div.head: In Cn III 55
div.ab: Comitis rectitudines secundum Anglos istę sunt communes cum rege: tertius denarius in uillis ubi mercatum conuenerit et in castigatione latronum; et comitales uillas quę pertinent ad comitatum eius; et consuetudines liberalium hominum duppliciter omnes habere, uidelicet duplicem mundam, duplicem manbote et forisfacturam (duplicem); duplex etiam habere debet prętium, id est þere.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 614–615 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

den tertius denarius placitorum comitatus giebt dem Grafen Domesday für York-, Lincoln-, Nottingham- und Derbyshire. Im 12. Jh. verlieh ihn Königsurkunde, keineswegs in allen Grafschaften: Comes .. tertiam portionem eorum que de placitis proueniunt in comitatu quolibet percipit; ... set hii tantum, .. quibus regum munificentia ... decernit; [Ric. fil. Nigelli] Dial. de scaccario I 17 um 1178; vgl. Round 293

Domesday gives the earl the tertius denarius placitorum comitatus for York-, Lincoln-, Nottingham- and Derbyshire. In the 12th cent. it was granted by royal charter, by no means in all counties: Comes .. tertiam portionem eorum que de placitis proueniunt in comitatu quolibet percipit; ... set hii tantum, .. quibus regum munificentia ... decernit; [Ric. fil. Nigelli] Dial. de scaccario I 17 c. 1178; cf. Round 293
